newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Total to drill in Irish Porcupine Basin.
newsitem.headline: Total to drill in Irish Porcupine Basin.

text.p: French energy group Total SA is to drill an oil exploration well in Porcupine Basin, off the south-west coast of Ireland, Minister for Public Enterprise Mary O'Rourke said on Thursday.
The well will be located in block 35/17, about 150 km off the coast of Kerry, O'Rourke said in a statement.
Total will be drilling under their frontier exploration licence, granted in 1995. Total's partners in the three and a half block licence are DSM Energy and DuPont Co's unit Conoco.
Marathon also plans to drill an exploration well in the Porcupine Basin this year and expectations are that the well should commence in late July or early August, O'Rourke said.
Enterprise Oil will drill an exploration well in the Kish Bank Basin, offshore Dublin, toward the end of the year.

Statoil, which holds a lease undertaking over the Connemara Field, also in the Porcupine Basin, is currently conducting a two-well appraisal programme to determine whether oil can be produced on a commercial basis.
Current plans are that the company will produce oil on an extended well test starting later this month.
